thread:
elaine (Design): quick one — attaching a mock for the 'safety net' modal that appears when someone tries to rollback a canary. want UX + a11y eyes. modal has two CTAs: primary destructive and a safer secondary. screenshot: https://figma.mock/rollback-modal-1

matt (Product): looks cleaner than before. quick Q — should the secondary be 'Cancel rollback' or 'Keep current'? 'Cancel rollback' feels more action-y.

elaine (Design): i tried both. 'Cancel rollback' reads like it closes the dialog without implying the system stays on the current version. 'Keep current' is explicit, but longer. alternatives: 'Abort rollback', 'Stop rollback', 'Keep current version'. open to concision tradeoffs.

aria (Accessibility): a couple of a11y flags: 1) destructive action as primary can be risky — recommend styling it destructive but default keyboard focus on the safe action. 2) add aria-describedby describing consequences (e.g., which version and rough ETA). 3) ensure color contrast for destructive button text >= 4.5:1.

raj (Eng Runtime): backend note: if rollback is immediate we should show an estimated time to completion. we can include a placeholder token `{eta}` populated by API. also we can return the exact version id to mention in the modal.

toni (PM): +1 to showing ETA. also want a tiny timeline spark inside the modal showing the last 3 versions so folks understand what they're reverting to (compact, not interactive). is that feasible?

sam (Design): pushed an updated mock: moved safe action to the left, added a mini timeline bar (3 ticks) and tightened copy. changed primary label to 'Rollback now', secondary to 'Keep current'. contrast tweak on the red. https://figma.mock/rollback-modal-2

matt (Product): 'Rollback now' reads strong and clear. worried about length of 'Keep current' on small screens — maybe 'Keep current' is ok, but test truncation.

aria (Accessibility): mobile stacking note: when buttons stack, the safe action should be first (top) to match focus order. also add hidden explanatory text for screen readers: 'This will revert traffic to v1.2.3 and may take about 2 minutes.'

elaine (Design): added visually-hidden sentence and updated focus order in spec. also added an aria-label example: `<button aria-label="Rollback to v1.2.3 (estimated 2 minutes)">Rollback now</button>`.

raj (Eng Runtime): about the mini timeline: we can surface last 5 deployments from the page payload (no extra DB call on rollback path). endpoint we already use: `/api/deployments?service=svc-x&limit=5`. i'll add `recent_versions` to the page data.

toni (PM): perfect. devs — can you preload that so the modal doesn't need an extra fetch? @raj

raj (Eng Runtime): yes, will add it. ETA: midweek.

sam (Design): tiny visual nit — the active dot in the timeline was green on grey and fails contrast on hover states. i adjusted to a darker green + 2px outline.

aria (Accessibility): good. also please ensure focus ring is visible and meets contrast for the outline color.

raj (Eng Runtime): implemented the page payload change in a branch and added a small mock API response for `{recent_versions}`. code snippet: ```json
{"recent_versions":[{"version":"1.2.3","ts":"..."},{"version":"1.2.2"},{"version":"1.2.1"}]}
```

elaine (Design): thanks — i'll update Figma and the handoff doc. i also added a short QA checklist for accessibility: keyboard focus, screen reader announcement, contrast checks, and mobile CTA order.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch `design/rollback-modal-aria` to staging at 2024-09-14T15:26:45Z :rocket:

matt (Product): will review staging after the deploy. once validated, we'll slot it into next week's patch.

aria (Accessibility): i'll do a quick pass on staging after matt and post any issues.

elaine (Design): nice collab — i'll mark the Figma file as ready for dev. final microcopy we landed on: primary `Rollback now`, secondary `Keep current`. added hidden sr text with version + ETA. :white_check_mark:
